why: seeded-b's no-surge pool is replaced, never updated in place, when the lagging minor rolls: an in-place update drains the node, the budget planted on it holds that drain for an hour and the provider times out at thirty minutes, while a delete does not respect the budget and the replace takes minutes (defects-b.tf, the pool's lifecycle comment; the README's pin paragraph)

the scaled-zero-gateway fixture's status writer (defects-a.tf) is replaced whenever gateway_status.py changes or its GatewayClass, Gateway or HTTPRoute is created or replaced, so a re-created object gets the controller status no controller writes; the resource holds no state of its own, and the replace re-runs gateway_status.py

seeded-a's ConfigConnector writer (config-connector.tf) is replaced whenever config_connector.py or the object's spec changes, seeded-a is re-created (its CA certificate is a trigger), or a failed run taints it; the resource holds no state of its own, and the replace re-runs config_connector.py, a server-side apply that is safe to repeat

the orphaned-snapshot fixtures' planter (main.tf) is replaced whenever orphan_snapshot.py, the source disk's name or a snapshot name changes, on every plan whose probe reads a snapshot missing or the source disk present (the probe stamps such a reading with its time, so a recurrence is never read as the stored trigger), or after a failed run taints it; the resource holds no state of its own, and the replace re-runs orphan_snapshot.py, which takes only a snapshot that is missing, deletes only disks of the throwaway source's name, in any zone, and never touches an existing snapshot, so a re-run does not restart the check's 91-day clock; the run after a repair plans one more replace, a no-op, when the probe reads the repaired state
